answer: Each identity registers one summit crystal seam and locks a 70-credit bond, then a pulse-counted drill logs every pulse to the summit ledger under its key. The auditor recomputes crystal yield from the pulse count and releases the bond when logged pulses, seam record, and claimed yield all agree. The first drill permit costs 30 credits; the k-th costs 30+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6024 and 1000 fakes pay 3,027,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-drill ring fails because a reused drill log is already on the ledger and burns both bonds. An honest miner pays 30 once and recovers the bond.
